subject: combine stratum level density estimates outside distance

messages.author: be2485b0836d6632
messages.subject: combine stratum level density estimates outside distance
parts:
Hi,

I have calculated density estimates at stratum level, using covariate distance sampling, with covariates at stratum and observer level. I'd like to be able to combine some of these stratum level estimates (representing a higher level gouping of geographical sites) to obtain mean estimates with confidence intervals. Is it possible to do this using just the distance outputs (eg. stratum levels estimates, standard errors, sample sizes)? I'm asking because it may be easier to do this in R with the distance outputs rather than doing the analysis again using different arrangements of stratification.

thanks for your help,

Christian Devenish

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] combine stratum level density estimates outside distance
parts:
Christian

It should be possible to perform your higher level estimation by hand (with the help of R) in the case of strata being geographic.  Essentially, the density at the "higher level" is the average of the component densities.  However this average is a weighted average, most commonly weighted by the areas of the component strata.

The other component of this re-aggregation is whether there are dependencies between components.  Dependencies have consequences for the calculation of variance, hence confidence intervals. If the component estimates are all estimated independently, calculations are easy.  Calculations are made mildly more complicated if, for example, a common detection function was used for multiple strata, hence there is an induced dependency between strata. 

Section 3.7.1 of Buckland et al. (2001) provides a set of formulae for coping with variance calculations in the face of dependency.  Have a look there and get back to us if the information in the text does not cover your situation.

How would I substitute effort for Area? Do you have a formula (or code) for this case?

Cheers,
Christian

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] combine stratum level density estimates outside distance
parts:
Christian

Comments on your 4 questions:

  • weighting by effort rather than area: if the stratification is geographic, I would stay with area weights

  • comment about f(0): I presume you are referring to Eqn 3.123 for where the second term in brackets is CV(h(0)), you would replace CV(h(0)) with CV(f(0)). You are missing an exponent 2 for your denominator of CV(f(0)).

  • substituting effort for area: in Eqns. 3.122, 3.123 and 3.125 the would be stratum-specific effort rather than stratum-specific area

  • code: I likely coded something 8-9 years ago, but unfortunately that was about 3 hard disks ago.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] combine stratum level density estimates outside distance
parts:
Christian

There is a transformation between variance of encounters per transect and variance of encounter rate (mentioned just below Eqn. 3.78 in Buckland et al. (2001:79)

The encounter rates (and their variances) are reported in the Distance output, but you want to use in your “higher level of aggregation” variance estimates.
